name: a or the
rule: Use 'a' for any one thing, met for the first time.
Use 'the' for a thing already mentioned, or the only one there is.

wrong.text: I bought a kite and a ball. A kite broke on the first day.

right.text: I bought a kite and a ball. The kite broke on the first day.

spot: Has the thing come up before, or is there only one? Then it is 'the'.
deeper: Only one: the sun, the sea, the principal of our school.
With the -est words: the tallest, the best.
With a plain job or kind: she is a nurse.

extra.text: Dad found an old radio in the store room. He said a radio still worked.
extra.note: It is the same radio, already mentioned, so it is 'the radio'.

extra.text: On the trip, we watched a sun set slowly behind the hills.
extra.note: There is only one sun, so it is 'the sun'.

extra.text: Mei won the race and then gave a medal to her grandmother.
extra.note: It is the medal she just won, so it is 'the medal'.
